case_title: Dilip Sudhakar Pendse & Anr. v. Central Bureau of Investigation
trial_court_outcome: Case committed to Court of Session for trial
neutral_facts: The appellants were prosecuted for alleged offences punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471, and 477-A of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 120-B. A charge-sheet was filed against the appellants and others in the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's court. One of the accused turned approver, and the Magistrate granted him pardon and committed the case to the Court of Sessions for trial. The Sessions Judge held that the offences were not exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions and sent the case back to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate for trial. The High Court, however, directed the matter to be tried by the Court of Sessions. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court's order and restored the proceedings to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate for trial.
